title: Round 29 Kentucky-Tennessee state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for Kentucky and Tennessee. Every seeded row reproduces one USGS GNIS record screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned GNIS primary point, and cross-checked on two independent USGS surfaces (USGS GNIS Geocoder; staged-products DomesticNames text via tools/gnis_extract.py; cumulative candidate extract resources/city-subsurface/gnis-candidates-batch7.json with per-state ZIP SHA-256 values). Black Mountain and Mount Le Conte additionally carry Domestic Names per-ID identity checks. The Ohio River is seeded for the first time in this batch: its main-stem record is Kentucky-associated. Kuwohi/Clingmans Dome is recorded as a cross-state context decision.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature and the point lay inside the intended state. County/census divisions, merged metro-government records, historical places, and same-name records of another class or county were rejected explicitly where relevant.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Second-surface cross-check of every seeded FEATURE_ID and per-ID identity checks for Black Mountain (510753) and Mount Le Conte (1646824), extracted in a GitHub Actions runner by tools/gnis_extract.py. The current text layout carries no elevation columns, so the two summit elevations cite USGS-published values. The candidate extract file is cumulative across batches 7-12; this register is the frozen batch-12 evidence.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service, reproduced identically on the second USGS surface.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake for the accepted named lakes and reservoirs (the extract's text class for the batch-12 lake rows is Reservoir), Streams & Canals to Stream, and Summit to Summit.
A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit outline, or river centerline.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, or the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor.
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

Kentucky.title: Kentucky statewide frame (Kentucky-Tennessee batch)
Kentucky.frameNote: Kentucky-Tennessee batch: the Frankfort capital anchor is balanced with the per-ID Black Mountain high point, the Cumberland/Barkley reservoirs, and four river mouth records (Ohio, Tennessee, Cumberland, Kentucky). This batch resolves the Ohio River: after empty states=OH/IN/IL/PA screens, its main-stem record proves Kentucky-associated and is seeded once here at its Mississippi-confluence mouth. The Tennessee and Cumberland mouth records are likewise Kentucky-associated (both empty under TN) and seeded here. Kentucky Lake's record is Tennessee-associated (seeded in Tennessee).

tennessee.title: Tennessee statewide frame (Kentucky-Tennessee batch)

identityDecisions.candidate: Ohio River, FEATURE_ID 425264 (Ballard County mouth record)
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded in Kentucky. After four consecutive empty state screens (OH, IN, IL, PA in rounds 25-27), the states=KY screen returns the main-stem stream record at its Mississippi confluence; the seeded point follows the series convention of seeding the cross-state feature once, in the frame whose surface owns the record. It remains a corridor in the four upstream frames (their registers already record the empty screens).
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The mouth point is not a channel centerline, thalweg survey, or state boundary.

identityDecisions.candidate: Tennessee River (517033) and Cumberland River (517018) mouth records
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded in Kentucky. Both mouths are in Kentucky (Ohio River confluences above Paducah and at Smithland); under states=TN the Tennessee name returns only pulp-mill pond records and the Cumberland returns an empty array, so both rivers remain corridors in the Tennessee frame.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The mouth points are not channel centerlines.

identityDecisions.candidate: Kuwohi / Clingmans Dome (6,643 ft) under states=TN
identityDecisions.decision: Not seeded. The Geocoder states=TN screen returned an empty array and the DomesticNames_TN_Text extract contains no Clingmans/Kuwohi record: the summit's GNIS record is North Carolina-associated. Tennessee's seeded summit is Mount Le Conte (1646824, Sevier County, 6,593 ft), the highest Tennessee-associated GNIS summit; the dome appears only as a context corridor marker whose note claims no GNIS point.
identityDecisions.knownServiceDiscrepancy: A state-line summit's single GNIS record is owned by the neighbouring state's extract; the 2024 Kuwohi renaming is noted but the record itself is not reproduced in Tennessee surfaces.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: No coordinate is stored for Kuwohi in the Tennessee frame.

identityDecisions.decision: Seeded in Tennessee. The states=KY exact-name screen returned an empty array for the same impoundment; the TVA reservoir's GNIS record is Tennessee-associated. It remains a context corridor in the Kentucky frame (partnered there with the seeded Lake Barkley).
identityDecisions.knownServiceDiscrepancy: A border reservoir returns under only one of its two states at the primary-point level; seeded once, in Tennessee (as with Lake Erie in Ohio and Bull Shoals in Arkansas).
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The seeded point is not a shoreline or the state-line segment of the reservoir.

knownLimitations: Kentucky and Tennessee are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.

The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence. Every seeded row was reproduced on the second USGS surface (staged-products DomesticNames text) at the same primary point.

The current DomesticNames text layout carries no elevation columns, so Black Mountain (4,145 feet) and Mount Le Conte (6,593 feet) elevations cite USGS-published values; GNIS identity rests on the per-ID class/county/point reproduction. Kuwohi's 6,643 feet is general-knowledge context only and carries no stored coordinate.
GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain or corridors. Both frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines.
State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. Both rectangles include areas outside their state outlines; no boundary geometry is claimed.
